【原视频简介】
Every hunter has one of these buried in the freezer — a whole frozen venison shoulder that nobody really wants to deal with. But what if you don't thaw it at all?
I took a rock-solid venison shoulder straight from the deep freezer, put it into a cast-iron Dutch oven, and used a cooking method with roots going back nearly 90 years. Old U.S. government and military references suggested cooking meat from frozen wasn't nearly as crazy as it sounds.
I wasn't convinced.
The result genuinely surprised me. Tender, moist venison, bacon mashed potatoes, green beans and homemade gravy — all starting with a frozen-solid deer shoulder.
Frozen Venison Shoulder — Dutch Oven Method

Amazon Links:
Cast Iron Dutch Oven: https://amzn.to/3UCUd8w

Henckels Chef Knife: https://amzn.to/4xrZ6jo

Ingredients
1 whole bone-in venison shoulder, frozen solid
1 package bacon
Kosher salt
Coarse black pepper
Garlic powder
Onion powder
Rosemary
Thyme
2–3 onions, roughly chopped
Carrots, roughly chopped
Celery, roughly chopped
Garlic
Better Than Bouillon Beef Base
Water
Worcestershire sauce
Butter, as needed
Flour, for gravy
The Method
Start with the venison shoulder completely frozen. Mine came directly from the deep freezer and was roughly 20°F.
